items.criterion: Legitimate users can log in during a bot/login flood
items.scope: Recorded isolated local profiles; not a current deployed guarantee
items.detail: Bounded 30-second, 24-source attack; legitimate/victim sign-ins succeeded. Small login samples do not certify p99 or arbitrary-overload/shared-NAT availability.

items.criterion: Abuse is throttled before unbounded hash/DB consumption
items.scope: Recorded isolated local profiles; not a current deployed guarantee
items.detail: Recorded attack: 434 attempts, bounded native hashing, challenge/throttle responses and no failed-login account/session writes. Guards retain secure hashing cost.

items.criterion: No cross-tenant leakage is observed in tested scenarios
items.scope: Recorded isolated local profiles; not a current deployed guarantee
items.detail: Live tenant predicates, cross-shop negative controls, concurrent reads/writes and independent catalog keys are covered. This is not proof for every possible future route.

items.criterion: Public menus stay responsive at the tested local peak
items.scope: Recorded isolated local profiles; not a current deployed guarantee
items.detail: Three-shop menu/detail spikes and mixed-read headroom are recorded; the eventual hosted lunch-rush peak remains to be established. Small spike cohorts are diagnostic, not SLO tail proof.

items.criterion: Concurrent order bursts preserve prices and critical-record uniqueness
items.scope: Recorded isolated local profiles; not a current deployed guarantee
items.detail: 34 logical submissions produced 27 orders/54 lines including duplicate replays. Transaction conflict rollbacks are recorded separately from final logical success.

items.criterion: DB connections respect pool AND provider limits
items.scope: Local pool gate verified; actual provider quota unverified
items.detail: Configured local per-process/combined pool bounds pass. Hosting/provider quota, replica count plus rolling surge, administrative reserves and Supavisor limits must be verified against the selected deployment; local max_connections is not that quota.

items.criterion: No sustained memory/connection leak was observed in the recorded soak
items.scope: Recorded isolated local profiles; not a current deployed guarantee
items.detail: 60-minute profile passed. Combined 180-minute traffic plus targeted monitor correction supports the requested leak criteria. The original aggregate-count gate remains failed; the shortened corrected repeat remains incomplete. No fresh corrected three-hour or current-revision longevity claim.

items.criterion: p95/p99 and error budgets are explicitly recorded for critical finite routes
items.scope: Recorded isolated local profiles; not a current deployed guarantee
items.detail: Explicit catalog includes payment creation, order confirmation/rejection and preparation writes. Targets are defined; measured attainment, sufficient samples and browser/realtime targets remain separate.

items.criterion: Spikes/dependency faults recover without manual business-data repair
items.scope: Recorded isolated local profiles; not a current deployed guarantee
items.detail: Spike queues drain; restored DB/network/SDK dependencies accept new requests. Rollback, safe errors and fixture cleanup are verified; hosted failover/disaster recovery is separate.

items.criterion: Versioned stress evidence and rerun commands exist
items.scope: Recorded isolated local profiles; not a current deployed guarantee
items.detail: Recovery reporting is rerunnable with source/environment/seed/profile metadata and comparisons. Each domain stress profile also has its own rerun command; the one-row recovery workload does not replace real menu/login/order/soak tests.

limitations: Historical profiles retain their original dates, source schemas and scopes. This command does not rerun stress traffic or prove all tests pass on the current revision.
Provider limits and hosted peak traffic are not inferred from local PostgreSQL or synthetic data.
The combined soak verdict preserves failed/incomplete diagnostic runs rather than relabeling them.
Auth abuse/challenge state remains single-owner; multiple auth replicas and strict fleet-wide quotas require shared coordination.
